ui.purpose: All prose, table cells, nav, form copy. The default register.

label.purpose: Section headers, table column headers, badge text, stat labels. Always uppercase with tracking.

mono.purpose: Job output panel, file paths, inline code, .env key names. Only for machine-generated or machine-readable text.

motion.name: opacity-hover
motion.purpose: Button hover — opacity 1 → 0.85. The only interactive transition.

motion.name: slider-toggle
motion.purpose: Toggle switch track and thumb. System-convention timing.

motion.name: spinner
motion.purpose: Running-job indicator. Only appears during active pipeline work.

narrative.overview:
This interface is a classified-grade analyst's workspace. Raw transcripts and meeting notes flow in through a background pipeline; distilled obligations, decisions, and program signal emerge on screen. The design premise is that the analysis is the product — the interface exists only to surface it with zero friction and maximum legibility. In a tool this personal and this operational, every pixel that isn't carrying signal is overhead.

The palette is near-black with surgical precision accents. Category signals (EXEC, SOLUTION, DAILY, overdue acts) are color-coded in the same semantic vocabulary across every surface — once learned, a glance at the file table communicates the morning's meeting mix before a single word is read. Depth comes from tonal layering, not shadows: the hierarchy is --bg → --surface → foreground, and you always know where you are in it.

Interactive components are precise and considered. Buttons have a hair of transition on hover; badges use deeply-saturated-but-dark backgrounds that read clearly without shouting. Nothing moves unless it's earning its motion — the spinner on a running job, the scroll auto-advance in the output panel.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black field (#0f1117) as the absolute base — the screen recedes
Semantic color vocabulary: six named signal colors, each owned by a single role
Flat tonal layering, no drop shadows anywhere
11px uppercase tracked labels for all section headers and table columns
SF Pro Text / system-ui as the sole prose face; SF Mono exclusively for code and live job output
Dense information layout — 14px base size, 1100px content cap, no wasted whitespace

rules.name: The One Hue, One Role Rule
rules.body: Each signal color — blue, green, orange, red, purple, cyan — is owned by exactly one semantic role. Never repurpose --accent for decoration, never use --green for anything other than success/confirmation, and never use --red for anything other than urgency/danger.

rules.name: The Neutral Majority Rule
rules.body: At least 90% of any given screen surface uses only the four neutral tokens. Signal colors are the 10% that earns attention by being rare.

rules.name: The Uppercase Label Rule
rules.body: Organizational text — card section headers, table column headers, badge text, stat labels — is always 11px uppercase with letter-spacing. Body text is never uppercase.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Drop shadows are permanently absent. When a surface needs to read as elevated, it uses --surface background against a --bg surround, optionally framed by a 1px --border outline. Adding shadows is a hard regression.

rules.name: The Consistent Rounding Rule
rules.body: Radius tier is determined by component class: cards are always 8px, buttons/inputs are always 6px, badges are always 4px. Never mix tiers within the same element or use ad-hoc values.

dos: Do use --accent (#4f8ef7) for all and only interactive affordances — links, focus rings, primary buttons, active nav state.
Do keep table rows at 7px vertical padding. Denser obscures; looser wastes the density advantage.
Do use SF Mono only for machine-generated or machine-readable text: job output, file paths, inline code, .env key names.
Do keep the stat tile value at 22px bold — it's the only large text in the system.
Do use the dark-tinted badge pattern (dark saturated background + colored text) for all new semantic badge types.
Do make the OVERDUE badge (#4a1010 / --red bold) the most visually prominent badge.
donts: Don't add box-shadows. The depth model is tonal. Any shadow is a regression.
Don't introduce new accent colors. The six signal colors are complete: blue, green, orange, red, purple, cyan.
Don't use color for decoration. Every non-neutral color on screen must carry semantic meaning.
Don't mix radius tiers within a component. Cards are 8px. Buttons/inputs are 6px. Badges are 4px.
Don't use uppercase for body text. The uppercase register is exclusively structural.
Don't auto-reload the page after a failed job. The output panel must stay visible when returncode !== 0.
